statement: Banked gold is the objective; banked iron is the first tiebreak.
limitations: Carried resources affect later tiebreaks, not the primary gold score.

statement: The pass-only starter submitted 480 passes in the first supplied match.
limitations: Action export alone is not a final scoreboard.

statement: Three workers beat one/two in the original simplified solo model.
limitations: Does not establish optimal worker count under opponents or all maps.

statement: Nearest gold plus fuller-load behavior beat the original rate/partial-return variant on 12 toy seeds.
limitations: Target selection and return policy changed together.

statement: An incoming worker could reserve ore and make an on-site miner idle; miner priority fixes the focused scenario.
limitations: Score benefit needs competitive validation beyond the toy model.

statement: Workers do not block movement and cannot hand cargo to one another under supplied actions.
limitations: Shared routes and rich deposits can be useful; overlap alone is not waste.

statement: A base claims ore within Manhattan distance two; overlapping claimants may all mine it.
limitations: Building nearby does not automatically deny an already-claiming opponent.

statement: V3 second-base policy improved the initial solo base test.
limitations: Simplified 30x30 solo model, no official win-rate inference.

statement: V4 coordinated ore assignment had mixed training and fresh-seed results.
limitations: Mean difference was small relative to paired variation; newer is not necessarily better.

statement: V5 reactive behavior checks pass, while its familiar solo mean did not beat V4.
limitations: Opponent-response heuristics were not measured by solo engines.

statement: V5 won the latest shared official practice game with 204 gold versus 188 for second.
limitations: Single uncontrolled map/roster; not proof of a better win rate.

statement: V6 route-priced base funding shows small uncertain gains over V5 in two simplified settings.
limitations: No official V6 outcome supplied; uncertainty exceeds the small mean gains.

statement: Center-directed exploration reduced returns on the initial rich-center test and is disabled.
limitations: Specific tested policy and model; not proof that the rich center is unimportant.

statement: Garrett attempted an extra base on turn 41 and repeated eight-mine/two-move/one-deposit loops.
limitations: Exact locations, successful resource types and score are absent; compact-hub interpretation is an inference.

statement: Garrett mine attempts declined from 221 in the first half to 115 in the second.
limitations: Local depletion/longer travel is a hypothesis, not confirmed hidden state.

statement: Garrett mined on turns 479 and 465 with two workers that never deposited afterward.
limitations: Those attempts cannot add banked gold; successful carried resources may affect later tiebreaks.

statement: The 193-gold V3 match lost on banked iron, 4 versus 6.
limitations: Late iron collection should not sacrifice profitable gold; no special tiebreak policy is shipped.

statement: Match a64dfc31 source attribution is unresolved: its build/trade actions cannot come from the supplied V1 snapshot.

statement: The ca31db86 BYU strategy was the teammate's separate code.
limitations: Its source was not supplied; do not blame or credit the archived chat bot versions for its actions.

statement: Scarcity mining priority uses eligible mining streak, then time on tile, then seeded tie order.
limitations: Faster submission does not improve this priority.

statement: The teammate's fourth worker made 38 mine attempts and 354 moves.
limitations: Construction work and actual output are unknown; this does not establish negative return.

statement: Telemetry covers strategy-delivered states and can be partial.
limitations: V3 log ends at 189; last observed state is distinct from final scoreboard.

statement: V5 banked all observed extracted gold and suffered three failed mines but no failed moves in its winning match.
limitations: Some failures may arise from opponents building/claiming or mining in the same turn; not every failure is predictable.

statement: A mining loop with eight successful gold mines, two moves and one deposit delivers eight gold in eleven worker-turns.
limitations: Assumes eligible gold, successful actions and no cooldown; Garrett's matching action pattern alone does not prove all assumptions.
